D10_adaptive_replication.concept: execute R_min replicas; stop if the observation is clearly away from the decision boundary; otherwise acquire further replicas up to R_max
conditions: the stopping rule is frozen BEFORE official generation and hashed into the replica protocol
the rule depends only on the observed successes so far and on frozen constants, never on any model output, label frequency or downstream outcome
the realized R becomes part of the candidate aggregate identity, so a row cannot be reproduced without knowing how many replicas it received
the likelihood used in training accounts for the stopping rule, or the rule is chosen so that the resulting likelihood is unaffected

consequences.budget: expected cost falls because most events stop at R_min, but worst-case cost is R_max everywhere and the budget must be declared against the worst case
consequences.event_weighting: UNAFFECTED IF the 1/R normalization is applied, which is exactly why that normalization matters more under adaptive R than under fixed R
consequences.identity: R is no longer a constant per family, so the aggregate identity must carry the realized R and the stopping-rule hash
consequences.matched_randomness: PRESERVED, because replicas are indexed by a counter PRF: COMPACT and LINE must acquire the SAME replica indices, which means the stopping decision must be taken jointly for the pair, not per candidate. A per-candidate stopping rule would break pairing and must be prohibited.
consequences.reproducibility: PRESERVED, because the stopping rule is deterministic given the frozen constants and the PRF-generated outcomes; a replay reaches the same stopping point
consequences.row_identity: rows are per (event, candidate, robot) and do not multiply with R, so row identity is unchanged apart from citing the new target contract

D10_adaptive_replication.recommendation: NOT recommended for the first V3 freeze. A fixed R is simpler to justify, and the measured compute budget shows no cost pressure that would motivate the added complexity. Recorded here as a viable later refinement.
D10_adaptive_replication.statistical_caveat: an optional-stopping rule can bias a naive point estimate of p. Under a binomial likelihood with a frozen, outcome-only stopping rule the likelihood is still proportional to p^k (1-p)^(R-k), so the estimator is unaffected; but this must be stated and justified prospectively rather than assumed

D26_calibration_bin_support.note: precision that matters for a probabilistic target is not per-event but per calibration bin, where many events pool

D9_what_R3_can_establish.0_of_3: one-sided only: p could be anywhere in [0, 0.7076]
D9_what_R3_can_establish.3_of_3: one-sided only: p could be anywhere in [0.2924, 1]
D9_what_R3_can_establish.conclusion: R = 3 CANNOT estimate a per-event probability. 1/3 and 2/3 are compatible with almost the entire unit interval. Any V3 target that requires PER-EVENT certainty about p is infeasible at R = 3.

decisive_asymmetry.cost_if_per_event_precision_is_required: R >= 27 for a +/-0.20 half-width and R >= 104 for +/-0.10, at every F8/F9 event -- prohibitive and still coarse
targets_not_needing_per_event_precision: C probabilistic with a binomial likelihood
decisive_asymmetry.why: a binomial NLL treats k out of R as a noisy but UNBIASED observation of p(x, tau). Consistency comes from the number of EVENTS, not from R within an event. Modest R is therefore statistically coherent for supervision even though it is useless for a single-event point estimate.

existing_v2_replicas_are_a_valid_prefix: because the stream is a counter PRF indexed by replica_index, replicas 0..2 of a larger set are exactly the existing three. Extending R re-uses them without recomputation ONLY if a prospective authorization says so and the identity contract records the new R.
method: exact Clopper-Pearson intervals by bisection on the binomial CDF; no normal approximation
recommended_R_rationale: R should be chosen to (a) keep the paired COMPACT/LINE comparison, (b) give enough distinct k/R levels for calibration-bin support, and (c) stay within budget. R = 3 gives only four levels {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1}; R = 5 gives six and R = 9 gives ten. This is an OWNER parameter, recorded here with its trade-off rather than selected.
